subject: Acceptance lag triage and critical-path reshuffle
messages:
From: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@helixhealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Acceptance window slip — updated timeline + impact

Hi Kimberly / Ben,

Quick note from Helix: the internal clinical QA team has pushed our acceptance window by two weeks — their new availability window starts the week of Jan 18. Attached is the latest evaluation timeline (EvaluationTimeline_v3.xlsx) they shared with dates highlighted.

Impact: this shifts our planned go‑live from Jan 31 to Feb 14 unless we compress the post‑eval cutover. Procurement also signaled they need the finalized SOW before Jan 10 to meet budget cycles.

Can your team share a short mitigation plan and whether Redwood can support a temporary canary deployment (limited accounts) to keep momentum?

Thanks,
Jordan Smith
Head of Integrations, HelixHealth
attachments: EvaluationTimeline_v3.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Acceptance window slip — updated timeline + impact

Jordan — thanks for the heads up and the timeline.

Short answer: we can support a two‑track approach: 1) rebaseline the MAP and stretch closed items into a phased acceptance plan, and 2) stand up a limited canary on a dedicated pool for the most critical customer segments.

Immediate asks from our side to finalize options:
- Confirm which Helix accounts must be included in the canary (top 3 by usage).
- Confirm procurement cutoff (you mentioned Jan 10) — we need that to lock licensing terms for the phased approach.
- Any evaluation must-have test cases (we saw a short list in the spreadsheet but need the full set).

I'll push a draft MAP rebaseline and a short risk log by EOD (internal). Ben — can you confirm GPU availability for a one‑week canary burst the week of Jan 11?

Best,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Strategic Account Manager, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@helixhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Dec 2026 10:25:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Acceptance window slip — updated timeline + impact

Kimberly — checking infra. Short response: we have a limited burst slot the week of Jan 11 but it consumes reserved capacity and will incur a short term premium. If Helix agrees to the phased MAP with a canary, I can carve the slot but we need procurement to confirm the purchase order by Jan 7 so finance can authorize the capacity bump.

If procurement can't meet that date, fallback is: compressed validation (parallel test runs) the week of Jan 18 and prioritized KV cache pre-warm to cut token latency at go‑live. That still means go‑live drifts to Feb 14.

Ben Carter
Customer Solutions — Redwood Dedicated
attachments: none
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Dec 2026 08:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Escalation: HelixHealth acceptance lag — request for credit / priority capacity

Marissa — flagging an exec‑level ask from Helix. Their budget cycle and QA availability are pushing the acceptance window out; procurement asks mean we risk losing momentum without a short credit or temporary priority capacity.

Summary of options I recommend we consider (tradeoffs included):
- Option A (preferred): Approve a small service credit to Helix and carve a Jan 11 canary slot. Pros: Keeps the go‑live target nearer Jan 31 for key accounts; preserves relationship. Cons: Short revenue impact and capacity reallocation.
- Option B: No credit; propose phased acceptance with Feb 14 go‑live and extended post‑acceptance support. Pros: Preserves revenue; Cons: risk of churn or reduced account enthusiasm.
- Option C: Approve priority capacity but require PO by Jan 7 (Ben can carve); if PO misses, fallback to Option B.

I've attached a draft rebaseline MAP and a one‑page risk log (MAP_proposed_rebaseline.pdf). Need approval on whether we offer a credit and how much — recommend a 10% short term credit tied to a committed support window.

Priyom Das
Director, Solutions & GTM Ops — Redwood Inference
attachments: MAP_proposed_rebaseline.pdf (pdf)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@helixhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 3 Jan 2027 16:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Acceptance window slip — updated timeline + impact

Thanks Priyom — reviewed. Approve Option C with a conditional credit: Redwood will reserve the Jan 11 canary slot and provide a one‑time 8% service credit contingent on Helix issuing a PO for the reserved capacity by end of day Jan 7. If PO is not received, we will shift to the phased MAP with new go‑live target Feb 14 and no credit.

Action items (owners + dates):
- Helix: confirm canary accounts and submit PO by 2027‑01‑07 (Jordan / Procurement).
- Kimberly: finalize rebaseline MAP and risk register; share to Helix + internal execs by 2027‑01‑04.
- Ben: confirm capacity carve and estimated overage cost; publish by 2027‑01‑04.
- Priyom: prepare conditional credit memo and update the HubSpot deal (HLX-2026-045) with the new terms by 2027‑01‑04.

Jordan — Kimberly will follow with the updated MAP and acceptance checklist. We want to signal flexibility while protecting Redwood economics.

Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
